annotations.text:
Today a new workspace is a window.prompt for a name.

This drafts the space instead: pick what it is for, get a first cut you can edit, then see exactly what lands on disk and on the clock before anything is written.

Five kinds — two lean Business, two lean Personal, one neutral.

The kind only chooses what gets drafted. It is not a new kind of node to live with: afterwards Fitness is a folder like any other, and the vault still derives kind from depth.

And the tag is not tied to the kind. It suggests; you decide.

The assistant drafts and explains, it does not interview. One line at the bottom redrafts what is above.

Same pattern as the bot: a blank form is a worse question than a wrong answer.
"Not created" is the half nobody states. Saying what will NOT happen is what makes the list above trustworthy — the same discipline as the bot page saying it will refuse every call.

The same screen, the other kind — the test for whether two kinds are really two.

Business gets Clients / Money / Marketing and a Monday-to-Friday rhythm on work hours. Personal gets areas and evenings. No repositories are assumed in either: a product goes in later as a folder, and becomes a project when you give it a repository.

The extra panel is the one thing a business space reaches for that a personal one usually will not — a command across every repository. Named, not drafted: a wrong command is worse than none.
